# The Scovant agent-readiness checks

This is the open specification of the checks Scovant Cloud runs on every
scan, generated from the same catalog that serves
[scovant.com/rules](https://scovant.com/rules) and the public JSON at
`https://scovant.com/api/public/rules`. The interactive scoring page is
[scovant.com/scoring](https://scovant.com/scoring).

- **65 rules** across 7 categories — 34 `required` (scored) and 31 `experimental` (reported, never scored).
- Ruleset version `c12293cd6d02` (sha256 over every rule's code and version; a new value means the model changed, and CI runs tell 'website changed' from 'model changed' apart).
- The open-source scanner [Scovant Core](https://github.com/Scovant/scovant-core) implements a
  separate, passive check set with its own public scoring — see its `docs/checks.md`.

## Scoring model

Every check produces an outcome for each page or for the domain: PASS, WARN or
FAIL when it could be measured, N/A when it does not apply to the site, and
NOT_MEASURED when its input was not available (for example our fetch failed).
Measured outcomes count PASS 1 · WARN 0.5 · FAIL 0; a check's weight follows its severity
(critical 40 · high 25 · medium 14 · low 6 · info 2). A category's score is the weighted share of its measured checks
that pass, plus a pseudo-pass with prior weight 14 so a
single failure in a category with few measured checks cannot drive it to 0; the
prior is not evidence and never counts toward coverage. The
overall rating is the weighted blend of the categories that have a score;
categories that don't apply to a site type (UCP for a blog, citability for a
shop) are excluded and the weights renormalize over the rest.

| Category | Weight | What it measures |
|---|---|---|
| discoverability | 0.17 | Can an agent reach and crawl the content at all — robots, AI-crawler access, bot protection, canonicals, llms.txt, crawl graph, agent identity |
| structured | 0.18 | Machine-readable product/offer data (schema.org Product, price, availability, variants) |
| consistency | 0.15 | Do prices / entities / structured data agree across the page and the DOM |
| actionability | 0.12 | The agent action surface — deep links to key pages, no JS-only critical content, MCP / WebMCP interfaces and their metadata |
| trust | 0.08 | Citation/transaction trust signals — returns policy, shipping info, OG meta, instruction-reference integrity |
| ucp | 0.12 | Universal Commerce Protocol — published profile, valid schema, checkout descriptor, signing keys (commerce-like and SaaS sites) |
| citability | 0.18 | Content sites only — is the prose self-contained and citable by AI search engines |

`experimental` checks are reported but never counted, whatever their severity —
they are visible so you can act on them, but they do not move the rating until
a dated, calibrated promotion to `required`.

Missing evidence is never counted as a failure — it lowers **coverage**, the share of
applicable weight that was actually measured. Below 85% coverage the
rating is shown without a grade or badge; below 60% there is no rating
at all (not enough evidence), rather than a number built on guesses.

The headline result is **Agent Readiness**: every check, plus what a real agent
experienced. **Technical Readiness** beside it uses the passive checks only. An
agent-blocking condition (an AI crawler refused by robots.txt, or bot protection
blocking our honest agent identity) holds Agent Readiness below the badge
thresholds — being unreachable to agents dominates everything else. The exact
value of that limit is part of the proprietary engine and is not published; see
the scoring page for what is and is not public.

Commerce-like sites (commerce / booking / restaurant) also get simulation-aware
scoring: real AI agents attempt the purchase flow and the outcome adjusts the
rating — a passing simulation lifts it, a failing one holds it below the badge
thresholds.

Grades: rating ≥ 90 → **A**; badges: ≥ 80 → **agent_ready** (grade B floor), ≥ 60 → **agent_compatible** (grade C floor); below that, D.

## The checks

Every row links to the rule's public page (what it detects, why it matters,
remediation, references). Maturity `experimental` = reported, not scored.
Source `core ≥ X.Y.Z` = computed by the open-source engine since that release
(pin it and you get the same verdict); `cloud` = needs Scovant's own
agent-identity fetch, which the open-source engine does not perform.
OWASP = the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026 categories a rule is
evidence about (every one `PARTIAL`). It is a mapping, not a compliance claim;
`—` = the rule maps to no category.

## Beyond static checks

The checks above are what a scan can verify from the outside. Scovant's
simulation layer goes further: real AI agents (a catalog of 15 LLM agents)
attempt actual purchase and booking flows, and CI integration compares every
deploy against a baseline so agent-readiness regressions are caught before agents
hit them in production. See [scovant.com](https://scovant.com) and the
[ci-examples](https://github.com/Scovant/ci-examples) repo.
